claims.text: A technical debt register lists the debt a team knows it carries: what it is, where it is, how it arose, what it costs each change, what repaying it would take, and who watches it.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 1; content/glossary.yaml technical-debt-register short_en; docs/team/tech-debt-register.md @ stage-3 line 16

claims.text: At stage-3, CreateOrderItemRequest in Dtos.cs still has UnitPriceVnd; an OrdersController.cs comment says it is accepted so older clients keep working but ignored, price taken from Catalog (owns product prices); one OrdersApiTests test sends UnitPriceVnd: 1.

At stage-3 the donhang database still holds old notifications and payments tables (rows N1, N2); PostgresFixture, the integration-test setup, still names them; the register's parenthesised numbers refer to decision records in docs/adr.
A risk may never happen, while a debt in the register already exists and charges interest on every change to that area, so rating its likelihood says nothing and it gets a list of its own.
Interest is written in the team's own words (what a reader is misled into, what extra step each change takes) rather than a score, because a score cannot be checked against what happens in a change.

Line 16 of tech-debt-register.md is the header with eight columns: Số, Món nợ, Ở đâu, Từ đâu ra, Lãi mỗi lần sửa, Trả bằng cách nào, Quyết định, Người theo dõi; lines 9-10 ask for interest in words; lines 10-12 list the four decision values.

Row N3 (line 20): POST /api/v1/orders still accepts each line's unitPriceVnd but ignores it; arose deliberately to keep old clients working; interest: a reader of the API thinks they can set the price, each DTO change must remember the field does nothing; watched by a backend developer.
N3 and N4 are marked 'Có chủ ý' (taken on purpose) in the Từ đâu ra column.

Repaid list (lines 23-28): T1 is the full manifest copy per environment, repaid in one commit checked against the difference Argo CD reported; T2 (QueuedNotifier, messaging work) also records what repayment took. Lines 32-33: reviewed with the risk register at each sprint planning.

The register is reviewed at the same rhythm as the risk register; a row still carried stays until the next review; a repaid item moves to a separate list with what the repayment took, which the team can consult when estimating a similar repayment.

A code comment is read only by whoever opens that file, cannot be reviewed with the rest, rarely names cost or watcher, and debt in data (an unused table) has no one file that whoever changes the schema is sure to open.
A register line with no concrete cost to changes is a complaint, not debt; each row needs interest, repayment and a watcher.
design.l3.one-way-module-dependencies is where order prices moved to Catalog; the OrdersController comment on unitPriceVnd is tagged with that lesson.
